original_question: Which type of inflammatory choroiditis, classified as part of the White Dot Syndromes, predominantly affects young myopic women and is characterized by a lack of inflammation in the anterior chamber and vitreous humor?

final_qi.question: Which type of inflammatory choroiditis, classified as part of the White Dot Syndromes, predominantly affects young myopic women and is characterized by a lack of inflammation in the anterior chamber and vitreous humor?
final_qi.search_keyword: inflammatory choroiditis White Dot Syndromes young myopic women lack inflammation anterior chamber vitreous humor
final_qi.long_answer: Punctate inner choroidopathy (PIC) is a form of inflammatory choroiditis that is commonly classified among the White Dot Syndromes. It primarily affects young myopic women and is distinguished by the absence of significant inflammation in the anterior chamber and vitreous humor. Unlike other inflammatory diseases of the eye that involve extensive intraocular inflammation, PIC typically presents with small, punctate lesions at the level of the choroid without the usual inflammatory markers in the front portions of the eye. This clinical profile helps differentiate PIC from other similar chorioretinopathies and is a key factor in its diagnosis and management.
